summary: Sample a remote clip into one filmstrip through an aggregate byte-capped Range-only view. Geometry in, one picture plus a closed transport receipt out.

parity.note: The decoder receives the origin's original compressed bytes and the exact media.filmstrip argv, including its measured duration, rounded seek timestamps, crop, scaler and PNG sink. Only the HTTP reader changes: every origin request is an explicit bounded Range and a shared block cache applies one aggregate byte cap across ffprobe plus all ffmpeg inputs. tests/test_op_media_range.py renders the ordinary full-file path and this path over the same real MP4 and compares the final PNG bytes. The required JSON receipt is closed and proves origin_bytes < object_bytes, whole_attempts=0, Range request count, ignored-Range refusals, cap refusal and output presence. An origin 200 is closed while still streamed, before any body byte is consumed; cap exhaustion and malformed Content-Range produce no strip and never fall back to a whole GET. No selection rule crosses: positions and cell geometry are the same surface as media.filmstrip.

url.description: Credential-free public origin location. Checked on every redirect before it is dereferenced.

positions.description: Fractions of the clip's own measured duration; geometry only, with no selection rule.

max_origin_bytes.description: Aggregate ceiling across discovery, probe and every decode input. The handler additionally clamps it below Content-Length, so no setting admits a whole object.
